open_points.subject: sandbox file-size-limit outcome
open_points.text: “the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error the code can see” conflicts with “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`”
open_points.question: If code catches or otherwise survives a scratch-file write failure caused by the file-size limit and returns conforming outputs, does `execute_function` return `resource_exhausted` or `succeeded`, and how is a caught or partially successful over-limit write detected?
options: Any attempted write past the limit makes the execution `resource_exhausted`, even if caught or partially written
Only an uncaught write error or abnormal exit makes the execution `resource_exhausted`; caught errors may still succeed
The write error is treated as an ordinary code exception, producing `crashed` when uncaught and allowing success when caught
open_points.default_guess: Record an out-of-band file-limit hit and return `resource_exhausted` even when the code catches the write error.
